{{short description|English applied mathematician}}
'''Susan North Brown''' (22 December 1937 – 11 August 2017) was a professor of mathematics at [[University College London]]<ref name="UCLNewsletter">{{cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/maths/news/2017/sep/dept-news-september-2017|title=Professor Susan Brown|date=8 September 2017|website=University College London}}</ref> and a leading researcher in the field of fluid mechanics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/maths/research/fluid-mechanics| website=UCL| title=Fluid Mechanics| date=24 May 2018|publisher=University College London}}</ref>

== Background and employment ==
An exact timeline for Susan Brown's career has been difficult to pin down, but a newsletter published by Department of Mathematical and Physical Sciences at [[University College London|UCL]] shortly after her death offers a framework for her career achievements and highlights the esteem in which she was held by colleagues and students.<ref name="UCLNewsletter"/> Her undergraduate degree in mathematics was from [[St Hilda's College, Oxford]].  For about two years more years she continued studies at Oxford, in theoretical [[fluid mechanics]]—and she then moved to the [[University of Durham]] to complete her DPhil in 1964.  During this time she held temporary Lectureships at both [[Durham University|Durham]] and [[Newcastle University|Newcastle]] and in 1964 began a Lectureship that started her long association with [[University College London|UCL]].  From her Lectureship she advanced to a Readership in 1971 and was appointed to a Professorship in 1986.  The [https://www.ucl.ac.uk/maths/news/2017/sep/dept-news-september-2017 afore-mentioned departmental newsletter] that recapped her accomplishments after her death expresses the belief that Brown was the first female in the UK to be appointed to a professorship in Mathematics, but [[Joan E. Walsh]] was promoted to a professorship in mathematics at the [[University of Manchester]] in 1974.<ref name="UCLWomenInMathematics">{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150516093028/https://www.ucl.ac.uk/maths/women-in-mathematics| url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/maths/women-in-mathematics|date=1 May 2015|title= UCL Women in Mathematics|archive-date=16 May 2015}}</ref>

== Research ==
Brown's department described her as an outstanding teacher and someone with an international reputation for her research.<ref name="UCLNewsletter" />  She had a productive partnership in fluid dynamics with [[University College London|UCL]] colleague [[Keith Stewartson]]—who also arrived at [[University College London|UCL]] in 1964. Quoting from the afore-mentioned departmental newsletter, " Together they published 29 papers and pioneered early developments of 'triple-deck' theory, which, in turn, enabled resolution of long-standing questions in steady and unsteady trailing-edge flows, and addressed associated important aerodynamic applications. Another area for which Brown was especially renowned was a series of discussions of critical layers, especially effects of viscosity and nonlinearity and applications to geophysical flows such as atmospheric jets."<ref name="UCLNewsletter" /><ref name="UCLWomenInMathematics" />  Google-[https://scholar.google.com/ Scholar] lists numerous papers for the pair "SN Brown, K Stewartson" and several of these are listed below.

==Death==
Brown died on 11 August 2017, aged 79, in [[London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/thetimes-uk/obituary.aspx?n=susan-north-brown&pid=186452746|title=Susan North Brown's Obituary on The Times|website=[[The Times]]}}</ref>
